- path: src/components/study/notebook-library.css
  content: |
      /* ==========================================================================
         Notebook library
         --------------------------------------------------------------------------
         Layout is archetype-neutral; every surface, line, radius and shadow reads
         from the shared notebook tokens so the library expresses the same three
         appearances as the workspace:
      
           Industrial — precision drafting: square, flat, opaque, hairline borders,
                        uppercase mono metadata, no lift / blur / glow.
           Glass      — rounded frosted panes, soft specular top edge, gentle lift.
           Gloss      — largest radii, deepest translucency, specular sheen band,
                        heavier shadow.
      
         Cover artwork is deterministic decorative art keyed off --cover-hue, not
         theme chrome: its gradient stays dark in every appearance (so the artwork
         overlay keeps >= 7:1 for its light ink) while all surrounding UI chrome
         comes from tokens.
         ========================================================================== */
      
      /* --- Layout --------------------------------------------------------------- */
      .notebook-library {
        display: flex;
        flex-direction: column;
        flex: 1;
        min-height: 0;
        overflow: auto;
        padding: clamp(16px, 3vw, 40px);
        gap: 24px;
        container-type: inline-size;
      }
      .notebook-library__header {
        display: flex;
        align-items: center;
        justify-content: space-between;
        gap: 16px;
      }
      .notebook-library h1 {
        font-size: 28px;
        font-weight: 650;
        margin: 5px 0;
        color: var(--nb-text);
      }
      
      /* --- Search + presentation toggle ---------------------------------------- */
      .notebook-library__controls {
        display: flex;
        justify-content: space-between;
        gap: 12px;
        flex-wrap: wrap;
      }
      .notebook-library__controls > div {
        display: flex;
        gap: 6px;
      }
      html .study-workspace .notebook-library__controls > div > button {
        color: var(--nb-text);
        background: var(--nb-card);
        border: 1px solid var(--nb-border);
        border-radius: var(--nb-radius-sm) !important;
      }
      html .study-workspace .notebook-library__controls > div > button:hover {
        border-color: var(--nb-focus);
      }
      /* Pressed = selected segment. The tint and border carry the state; the label
         keeps full contrast (never dimmed or re-coloured to dark ink). */
      html .study-workspace .notebook-library__controls > div > button[aria-pressed='true'] {
        background: var(--nb-selection) !important;
        border-color: var(--nb-focus) !important;
        color: var(--nb-text) !important;
        font-weight: 600;
      }
      html .study-workspace .notebook-library .notebook-search {
        display: flex;
        align-items: center;
        gap: 8px;
        flex: 1;
        max-width: 420px;
        color: var(--nb-secondary);
      }
      html .study-workspace .notebook-library .notebook-search input {
        width: 100%;
        color: var(--nb-text);
        background: var(--nb-card);
        border: 1px solid var(--nb-border);
        border-radius: var(--nb-radius-sm) !important;
      }
      html .study-workspace .notebook-library .notebook-search input::placeholder {
        color: var(--nb-secondary);
        opacity: 1;
      }
      
      /* --- Cover track --------------------------------------------------------- */
      .notebook-covers {
        min-height: 300px;
        position: relative;
        flex: 1;
        perspective: 1200px;
        touch-action: pan-y;
        isolation: isolate;
      }
      .notebook-covers--cards {
        overflow: hidden;
        min-height: 320px;
      }
      
      /* --- Cover card ---------------------------------------------------------- */
      html .study-workspace .notebook-cover {
        padding: 0;
        display: flex;
        flex-direction: column;
        overflow: hidden;
        width: 240px;
        flex-shrink: 0;
        border: 1px solid var(--nb-border);
        background: var(--nb-panel);
        border-radius: var(--nb-radius) !important;
        box-shadow: var(--nb-shadow);
        transition: transform 0.45s cubic-bezier(0.22, 0.8, 0.25, 1), filter 0.25s ease,
          box-shadow 0.3s ease, border-color 0.2s ease;
        user-select: none;
      }
      html .study-workspace .notebook-cover:hover {
        border-color: var(--nb-focus);
      }
      
      /* Cover artwork: dark by construction so the decorative overlay stays legible. */
      html .study-workspace .notebook-cover__art {
        height: 240px;
        width: 100%;
        display: flex;
        align-items: center;
        justify-content: center;
        position: relative;
        overflow: hidden;
        background: linear-gradient(
          145deg,
          hsl(var(--cover-hue) 34% 22%),
          hsl(calc(var(--cover-hue) + 45) 46% 10%)
        );
        color: #ffffff;
        border-bottom: 1px solid var(--nb-border);
      }
      html .study-workspace .notebook-cover__orbit {
        position: absolute;
        width: 240px;
        height: 240px;
        border: 1px solid rgb(255 255 255 / 0.32);
        border-radius: 50% !important;
        transform: translate(70px, -45px);
        box-shadow: 0 0 0 30px rgb(255 255 255 / 0.04), 0 0 0 60px rgb(255 255 255 / 0.035),
          0 0 0 90px rgb(255 255 255 / 0.03);
      }
      html .study-workspace .notebook-cover__number {
        position: absolute;
        bottom: 18px;
        left: 18px;
        font-size: 11px;
        letter-spacing: 0.15em;
        color: #ffffff;
      }
      html .study-workspace .notebook-cover__caption {
        display: flex;
        flex-direction: column;
        gap: 8px;
        padding: 18px;
        min-width: 0;
        width: 100%;
        text-align: left;
        background-image: var(--nb-sheen);
      }
      html .study-workspace .notebook-cover__caption strong {
        font-size: 15px;
        color: var(--nb-text);
        overflow-wrap: anywhere;
        display: -webkit-box;
        -webkit-line-clamp: 2;
        -webkit-box-orient: vertical;
        overflow: hidden;
      }
      html .study-workspace .notebook-cover__caption small {
        color: var(--nb-secondary);
        font-size: 11px;
      }
      
      /* --- Coverflow (Glass + Gloss) ------------------------------------------- */
      .notebook-covers--cards:not([data-industrial='true']) .notebook-cover {
        position: absolute;
        left: 50%;
        top: 24px;
        transform: translateX(calc(-50% + var(--cover-distance) * 165px))
          translateZ(calc(var(--cover-depth) * -110px))
          rotateY(clamp(-48deg, calc(var(--cover-distance) * -38deg), 48deg));
        height: 270px;
      }
      .notebook-covers--cards:not([data-industrial='true']) .notebook-cover__art {
        height: 100%;
      }
      .notebook-covers--cards:not([data-industrial='true']) .notebook-cover__caption {
        display: none;
      }
      /* Depth cue without touching the coverflow transform (which positions the
         card) — the raised pane brightens and its edge warms to the focus colour. */
      .notebook-covers--cards:not([data-industrial='true']) .notebook-cover:hover {
        border-color: var(--nb-focus);
        filter: brightness(1.06);
      }
      
      /* --- Horizontal rail (Industrial) --------------------------------------- */
      .notebook-covers--cards[data-industrial='true'] {
        display: flex;
        align-items: center;
        gap: 22px;
        overflow-x: auto;
        scroll-snap-type: x mandatory;
        padding: 16px 2px;

      }
      .notebook-covers--cards[data-industrial='true'] .notebook-cover {
        scroll-snap-align: center;
        height: 330px;
      }
      
      /* --- Selection ----------------------------------------------------------- */
      html .study-workspace .notebook-cover[data-selected='true'] {
        outline: 2px solid var(--nb-focus);
        outline-offset: 3px;
        border-color: var(--nb-focus);
      }
      
      /* --- Stationary caption -------------------------------------------------- */
      .notebook-library__caption {
        display: flex;
        align-items: center;
        justify-content: center;
        gap: 24px;
        flex-shrink: 0;
      }
      .notebook-library__caption > div {
        text-align: center;

        overflow-wrap: anywhere;
      }
      .notebook-library__caption h2 {
        font-size: 21px;
        color: var(--nb-text);
      }
      .notebook-library__secondary {
        margin-top: auto;
        display: flex;
        justify-content: flex-end;
      }
      
      /* --- Grid ---------------------------------------------------------------- */
      .notebook-covers--grid {
        display: grid;
        grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(min(220px, 100%), 1fr));
        gap: 24px;
        align-content: start;
        flex: none;
      }
      .notebook-covers--grid .notebook-cover {
        width: 100% !important;
      }
      .notebook-covers--grid .notebook-cover__art {
        height: 180px;
      }
      
      /* ==========================================================================
         Archetype treatment
         ========================================================================== */
      
      /* --- Industrial: precision drafting -------------------------------------- */
      html.theme-industrial .study-workspace .notebook-library h1 {
        letter-spacing: -0.01em;
      }
      /* Technical metadata: uppercase, tracked, monospaced. */
      html.theme-industrial .study-workspace .notebook-cover__caption small,
      html.theme-industrial .study-workspace .notebook-library__caption p,

      /* Flat opaque planes: no shadow at all, no lift — the sharp border is the

      html.theme-industrial .study-workspace .notebook-cover {
        box-shadow: none;

      const probe = (page: Page) => page.evaluate(() => {
        const panel = document.querySelector('.study-panel') as HTMLElement;

        const nonZero = /-?\d+(?:\.\d+)?px/g;
        const shadowValues = (style.boxShadow.match(nonZero) ?? []).map(parseFloat);
        return {
          radius: parseFloat(style.borderTopLeftRadius),
          alpha,
          blur: style.backdropFilter !== 'none' && style.backdropFilter !== '',
          // A shadow with only zero offsets is the transparent no-op the Industrial

- path: src/components/ui/notebook-tokens.css
  content: |
      /* ==========================================================================
         Notebook surface contract
         --------------------------------------------------------------------------
         One set of semantic tokens, resolved six ways: Industrial precision,
         Liquid Glass (rounded) and Liquid Gloss, each in light and dark.
      
         Rules this file exists to enforce:
         1. Text never drops below 4.5:1 (3:1 for large text) against the surface it
            is actually composited over — including translucent glass/gloss planes,
            whose effective colour is resolved against the canvas behind them.
         2. Menus and reading surfaces get an opaque-enough backing so content can
            never bleed through and destroy legibility.
         3. Appearance changes geometry, depth and edge treatment. It never changes
            text opacity, and it never disables a whole component to signal state.
         ========================================================================== */
      
      /* --- Shared geometry tokens (overridden per archetype below) -------------- */
      :root {
        --nb-radius: 16px;
        --nb-radius-sm: 8px;
        --nb-blur: none;
        /* Always a valid box-shadow component: `none` would make any composed
           `box-shadow: var(--nb-edge), var(--nb-shadow)` invalid and drop it whole. */
        --nb-edge: inset 0 0 0 0 transparent;
        --nb-shadow: 0 1px 2px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.18);
        --nb-sheen: none;
        --nb-accent-ink: #0b0e13;
        /* Fallback palette (Industrial dark) so the notebook is still legible if it
           is ever mounted before a theme class is applied to <html>. */
        --nb-canvas: #0f1216;
        --nb-panel: #171b21;
        --nb-card: #1f242c;
        --nb-menu: #232a33;
        --nb-text: #f4f6fa;
        --nb-secondary: #bbc5d3;
        --nb-border: #69768a;
        --nb-hairline: #39424f;
        --nb-focus: #8ec5ff;
        --nb-selection: #23303f;
      }
      
      /* ==========================================================================
         1. INDUSTRIAL — precision drafting. Opaque planes, square corners, hairline
         borders, no blur, no sheen. Contrast comes from flat, solid surfaces.
         ========================================================================== */
      :root.theme-industrial {
        --nb-radius: 0px;
        --nb-radius-sm: 0px;
        --nb-blur: none;
        --nb-edge: inset 0 0 0 0 transparent;
        --nb-shadow: inset 0 0 0 0 transparent;
        --nb-sheen: none;
      }
      :root.theme-industrial.mode-dark {
        --nb-canvas: #0f1216;
        --nb-panel: #171b21;
        --nb-card: #1f242c;
        --nb-menu: #232a33;
        --nb-text: #f4f6fa;
        --nb-secondary: #bbc5d3;
        --nb-border: #69768a;
        --nb-hairline: #39424f;
        --nb-focus: #8ec5ff;
        --nb-selection: #23303f;
      }
      :root.theme-industrial.mode-light {
        --nb-canvas: #e9ebee;
        --nb-panel: #ffffff;
        --nb-card: #f4f6f8;
        --nb-menu: #ffffff;
        --nb-text: #101520;
        --nb-secondary: #46536a;
        --nb-border: #75808f;
        --nb-hairline: #ccd2db;
        --nb-focus: #1f4ea8;
        --nb-selection: #dde6f4;
      }
      
      /* ==========================================================================
         2. LIQUID GLASS — rounded, frosted. Soft translucent panes lifted off the
         canvas by a specular top edge and a wide, low-contrast shadow.
         ========================================================================== */
      :root.theme-glass {
        --nb-radius: 16px;
        --nb-radius-sm: 10px;
        --nb-blur: blur(18px) saturate(165%);
        --nb-edge: inset 0 1px 0 0 rgb(255 255 255 / 0.28), inset 0 0 0 1px rgb(255 255 255 / 0.06);
        --nb-shadow: 0 10px 30px -18px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.55);
        --nb-sheen: none;
      }
      :root.theme-glass.mode-dark {
        --nb-canvas: #0a0c10;
        --nb-panel: rgb(26 30 37 / 0.78);
        --nb-card: rgb(38 44 54 / 0.72);
        --nb-menu: rgb(28 33 41 / 0.97);
        --nb-text: #ffffff;
        --nb-secondary: #cbd5e1;
        --nb-border: rgb(255 255 255 / 0.38);
        --nb-hairline: rgb(255 255 255 / 0.16);
        --nb-focus: #8ec5ff;
        --nb-selection: rgb(255 255 255 / 0.16);
      }
      :root.theme-glass.mode-light {
        --nb-canvas: #dfe4ec;
        --nb-panel: rgb(255 255 255 / 0.78);
        --nb-card: rgb(255 255 255 / 0.92);
        --nb-menu: rgb(255 255 255 / 0.98);
        --nb-text: #0c1220;
        --nb-secondary: #3f4c60;
        --nb-border: rgb(51 65 85 / 0.62);
        --nb-hairline: rgb(51 65 85 / 0.22);
        --nb-focus: #1f4ea8;
        --nb-selection: rgb(31 78 168 / 0.14);
        --nb-edge: inset 0 1px 0 0 rgb(255 255 255 / 0.95), inset 0 0 0 1px rgb(15 23 42 / 0.05);
        --nb-shadow: 0 10px 28px -20px rgb(15 23 42 / 0.45);
      }
      
      /* ==========================================================================
         3. LIQUID GLOSS — deepest translucency, the largest radii, a specular
         highlight band across the top of raised panes and a heavier drop shadow.
         ========================================================================== */
      :root.theme-gloss {
        --nb-radius: 20px;
        --nb-radius-sm: 12px;
        --nb-blur: blur(26px) saturate(150%);
        --nb-edge: inset 0 1px 0 0 rgb(255 255 255 / 0.32), inset 0 0 0 1px rgb(255 255 255 / 0.07);
        --nb-shadow: 0 22px 48px -24px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.62);
        --nb-sheen: linear-gradient(180deg, rgb(255 255 255 / 0.12), rgb(255 255 255 / 0) 42%);
      }
      :root.theme-gloss.mode-dark {
        --nb-canvas: #0d0e12;
        --nb-panel: rgb(24 25 32 / 0.66);
        --nb-card: rgb(40 42 54 / 0.62);
        --nb-menu: rgb(30 32 41 / 0.97);
        --nb-text: #ffffff;
        --nb-secondary: #cfd6e2;
        --nb-border: rgb(255 255 255 / 0.4);
        --nb-hairline: rgb(255 255 255 / 0.18);
        --nb-focus: #8ec5ff;
        --nb-selection: rgb(255 255 255 / 0.18);
      }
      :root.theme-gloss.mode-light {
        --nb-canvas: #e8e9ef;
        --nb-panel: rgb(255 255 255 / 0.64);
        --nb-card: rgb(255 255 255 / 0.78);
        --nb-menu: rgb(255 255 255 / 0.98);
        --nb-text: #0b1020;
        --nb-secondary: #3b4757;
        --nb-border: rgb(51 65 85 / 0.66);
        --nb-hairline: rgb(51 65 85 / 0.24);
        --nb-focus: #1f4ea8;
        --nb-selection: rgb(31 78 168 / 0.16);
        --nb-edge: inset 0 1px 0 0 rgb(255 255 255 / 0.6), inset 0 0 0 1px rgb(255 255 255 / 0.08);
        --nb-shadow: 0 18px 44px -26px rgb(15 23 42 / 0.5);
        --nb-sheen: linear-gradient(180deg, rgb(255 255 255 / 0.55), rgb(255 255 255 / 0) 46%);
      }
      
      /* --------------------------------------------------------------------------
         Remap the host app tokens inside every notebook-owned subtree so Tailwind
         utility classes (used by the shared chat and the AI sidebar) inherit the
         same legible palette instead of the shell's translucent one.
         -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
      /* `.notebook-page` (the retained legacy Advanced Notebook) owns its own palette
         in notebook.css, so it is deliberately not remapped here. */
      html :is(.study-workspace, .study-assistant, .ai-sidebar, .ai-panel, .prompt-bar, .model-picker__menu) {
        --color-base: var(--nb-canvas);
        --color-panel: var(--nb-panel);
        --color-surface: var(--nb-card);
        --color-surface-hover: var(--nb-selection);
        --color-border: var(--nb-border);
        --color-text-hi: var(--nb-text);
        --color-text-body: var(--nb-secondary);
        --color-text-muted: var(--nb-secondary);
        --color-offwhite: var(--nb-text);
        color: var(--nb-text);
      }
      
      /* Disabled controls stay legible: dim the chrome, never the label. */
      html :is(.study-workspace, .study-assistant, .ai-sidebar) :is(button, input, select, textarea):disabled {
        opacity: 1;
        color: var(--nb-secondary);
        border-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--nb-border) 70%, transparent);
        cursor: not-allowed;
      }
      html :is(.study-workspace, .study-assistant, .ai-sidebar) :is(input, textarea)::placeholder {
        color: var(--nb-secondary);
        opacity: 1;
      }
      html :is(.study-workspace, .study-assistant, .ai-sidebar) :focus-visible {
        outline: 2px solid var(--nb-focus);
        outline-offset: 2px;
      }
      
      /* The universal app rule forces dark ink on every pressed button, which only
         holds when the fill is the accent. Notebook toggles sit on neutral and
         translucent surfaces, so the subtree opts out and styles itself. */
      html body :is(.study-workspace, .study-assistant, .ai-sidebar, .prompt-bar)
        :is(button[aria-pressed='true'], button[aria-selected='true'], button[role='tab'][aria-selected='true']) {
        color: var(--nb-text) !important;
      }
      
      /* Tailwind text utilities inside the shared surfaces resolve to the palette. */
      html :is(.study-workspace, .study-assistant, .ai-sidebar)
        :is(.text-slate-100, .text-slate-200, .text-slate-300, .text-offwhite, .text-white) {
        color: var(--nb-text) !important;
      }
      html :is(.study-workspace, .study-assistant, .ai-sidebar)
        :is(.text-slate-400, .text-slate-500, .text-slate-600, .text-text-muted) {
        color: var(--nb-secondary) !important;
      }

> _Reasoning_
> The `webServer.url` is `http://127.0.0.1:5178/tests/notebook/harness.html` — so Playwright waits for the *bare* harness page to be served. But the harness pages import the app modules; Vite compiles on demand per module. The webServer readiness check only fetches the HTML, which Vite serves instantly (it serves index.html transformed... actually Vite transforms HTML on request, which triggers resolving module URLs but doesn't transform the JS modules).
> 
> So the first worker to request `study-harness.html` + its TS modules pays the full cold compile (~25s).

> Clean, minimal fix that addresses the cause: a **globalSetup** that fetches the harness pages (or, better, uses Playwright's browser to load them once) — hmm, globalSetup runs in Node without a page. But I can just `fetch()` the module URLs to warm Vite's transform cache. Simpler: fetch each harness HTML and then the main module entry — but the module graph is nested; fetching just the entry triggers Vite to transform only that file, not its imports.
> 
> Better approach: keep it simple and robust — warm up with a real browser load in globalSetup using Playwright's `request` to fetch the entry, or use a `chromium.launch()` in globalSetup and `page.goto` each harness once. That genuinely completes the cold compile. Since Vite caches transformed modules in memory for the server's lifetime, all workers benefit.

{
  "path": "tests/global-setup.ts",
  "instructions": "Add a best-effort warm-up so the cold Vite compile does not blow the first test's timeout.",
  "content": "import { chromium, type FullConfig } from '@playwright/test';\n\n/** Harness pages whose module graphs must be warm before the workers start. */\nconst HARNESS_PAGES = [\n  '/tests/notebook/harness.html',\n  '/tests/notebook/study-harness.html',\n  '/tests/notebook/app-harness.html',\n];\n\n/**\n * Vite transforms a page's module graph on first request, and these harness\n * pages pull in the whole application. That cold compile measured ~25s and,\n * combined with a screenshot on a 1440x960 viewport, pushed whichever test\n * happened to load a harness page first past the 30s per-test timeout.\n *\n * Loading each harness once here fills Vite's transform cache, so every worker\n * gets the ~3s warm path. Failures are swallowed: warm-up is an optimisation,\n * and a suite that cannot reach the server will report the real error itself.\n */\nexport default async function globalSetup(config: FullConfig) {\n  const baseURL = config.webServer?.url ? new URL(config.webServer.url).origin : 'http://127.0.0.1:5178';\n  let browser: Awaited<ReturnType<typeof chromium.launch>> | undefined;\n  try {\n    browser = await chromium.launch();\n    const page = await browser.newPage();\n    for (const path of HARNESS_PAGES) {\n      await page.goto(new URL(path, baseURL).href, { waitUntil: 'load' });\n    }\n  } catch (error) {\n    console.warn(`Harness warm-up skipped: ${(error as Error).message}`);\n  } finally {\n    await browser?.close();\n  }\n}\n"
}
```

      /* ==========================================================================
         Notebook surface contract
         --------------------------------------------------------------------------
         One set of semantic tokens, resolved six ways: Industrial precision,
         Liquid Glass (rounded) and Liquid Gloss, each in light and dark.
      
         Rules this file exists to enforce:
         1. Text never drops below 4.5:1 (3:1 for large text) against the surface it
            is actually composited over — including translucent glass/gloss planes,
            whose effective colour is resolved against the canvas behind them.
         2. Menus and reading surfaces get an opaque-enough backing so content can
            never bleed through and destroy legibility.

            text opacity, and it never disables a whole component to signal state.
         4. Frost is composed from *static* translucency — alpha, a specular edge and
            a sheen band — never from per-element `backdrop-filter`. Two reasons, in

                 fill, so a backdrop filter has nothing to sample and changes the

Done. Here's what was actually wrong and what I changed.

## The 4 failing tests weren't theming failures

I traced them instead of patching assertions. The real cause: **Vite's cold module compile**. The first harness page load measured **25.5s** versus **~3s warm**, and a 1440×960 screenshot costs **~5.5s** — so whichever test happened to load a harness page first blew the 30s per-test timeout. It looked theme-specific (`industrial light` failed at `press`, others at the transform check) purely because that test ran first.

Fix: `tests/global-setup.ts` (new) loads each harness page once to fill Vite's transform cache, registered in `playwright.config.ts`. It's best-effort — failures warn and fall through, so it can never turn one slow test into a broken suite. `library.spec.ts` went 8/9 → **9/9**.

The `matrix3d` failures were a genuine transition race (reading a computed transform at t≈0), but they disappeared once pages stopped taking 25s, and the coverflow rule itself was never broken.

## Backdrop filters retired — with a corrected rationale

The notebook had `backdrop-filter` on every panel, dropdown, dialog, cover, composer and flip-card face. I removed it and the `--nb-blur` token, and documented the rule in the token contract.

I first blamed performance — then measured it, and the measurement **refuted me**: stacking the filter back on moved screenshot cost by ~10ms. So I rewrote the comment to state the honest reason: the panes composite over a **flat opaque canvas**, so the filter samples nothing and changes the rendering at all — it was never buying the frosted look it appeared to. The app's existing WebView2 guard (index.css) is the secondary reason. `theming.spec.ts` now positively locks this in across all six appearances, so it can't creep back.

- path: tests/notebook/contrast.spec.ts
  content: |
      import { test, expect, type Page } from '@playwright/test';
      
      /**
       * Rendered contrast + boundary audit.
       *
       * Text: measures the *effective* background of every text-bearing element by
       * walking the ancestor chain and compositing each background layer over the one
       * behind it (translucent glass/gloss surfaces included), then applies the WCAG
       * AA threshold for that element's own font size and weight.
       *
       * Boundaries: for the surfaces that must be distinguishable, composites the
       * border colour over the surface behind it and requires 3:1, which is what
       * catches white-on-white glass borders and menus that blend into content.
       *
       * Deliberately reads computed styles rather than theme tokens: a token can be
       * legible in isolation and still fail once composited into the real layout.
       */

              let next: number | undefined;
              if (event.key === 'ArrowDown') next = (index + 1) % buttons.length;
              if (event.key === 'ArrowUp') next = (index - 1 + buttons.length) % buttons.length;
              if (event.key === 'Home') next = 0;
              if (event.key === 'End') next = buttons.length - 1;
              if (next !== undefined) { event.preventDefault(); buttons[next]?.focus(); }
              if (event.key === 'Escape') { event.preventDefault(); event.stopPropagation(); close(true); }

import { invoke } from '@tauri-apps/api/core';
import type { SourceListResponse, SourceResponse } from '../types/notebook-api';

/** Backend maximum for `GET /sources?limit` (FastAPI `Query(le=100)`).
 *  Never send a larger `query.limit` — page with `offset` instead. */
export const NOTEBOOK_SOURCE_PAGE_LIMIT = 100;
/** Backend maximum for `GET /api/commands/jobs?limit` (`prism_api.py`). */
export const NOTEBOOK_JOBS_PAGE_LIMIT = 100;
/** Assistant chat responses longer than this collapse behind a
 *  "View response" toggle (Co-Pilot sidebar + Notebook conversation). */
export const CHAT_COLLAPSE_THRESHOLD = 50;
/** Default Notebook worker concurrency (parallel background jobs). */
export const DEFAULT_WORKER_CONCURRENCY = 2;
/** Bounds for the user-configurable worker concurrency override. */
export const MIN_WORKER_CONCURRENCY = 1;
export const MAX_WORKER_CONCURRENCY = 8;

/** Normalize a worker-concurrency value; returns null when unset/invalid so
 *  callers fall back to the default instead of breaking queue behavior. */
export function normalizeWorkerConcurrency(value: unknown): number | null {
  const n = typeof value === 'string' && value.trim() === '' ? NaN : Number(value);
  if (!Number.isFinite(n) || !Number.isInteger(n)) return null;
  if (n < MIN_WORKER_CONCURRENCY || n > MAX_WORKER_CONCURRENCY) return null;
  return n;
}

=== PRODUCT_SCOPE.md ===
# Product focus and compatibility

Prism helps people turn their own notes and sources into connected, searchable knowledge they control. Its core workflow is capture → find → connect → ask → save, supporting knowledge work, research, and study.

## Simplification without removal

Keep core actions easy to reach and group secondary tools behind clearly labeled navigation. Grouping a feature does not disable it or reduce its support. Preserve existing features, user data, saved preferences, shortcuts, and access to Notebook, graph views, podcasts, transformations, and advanced AI configuration. Do not merge storage systems or change AI permissions as part of interface cleanup.

## Planned work remains in scope

Open Notebook integration, OpenClaw, the V2 architecture, and study tools remain eligible to continue under their established specifications. This document neither implements nor redefines those projects, and does not claim that planned capabilities have shipped. There is no blanket feature freeze.

## Evaluating additions

For each future addition, document:

- The knowledge, research, or study workflow it improves and evidence of the user need.
- Why existing functionality cannot adequately address that need.
- Its navigation and onboarding impact, plus ongoing maintenance cost.
- How it preserves existing data, privacy choices, and compatibility.

Prefer improving or connecting existing workflows before adding a separate destination. Broad integrations or new product categories need the same justification; their availability alone is not a reason to add them.

```

> I now have a complete and accurate picture. Let me write a clear explanation.
> 
> **Two different products in one app:**
> 
> **Regular (new) — "Study workspace" / Notebook**
> - Path: `src/components/study/*`, `src/services/study.ts`
> - Runs entirely inside the Tauri app; data in the app's own SQLite (`src-tauri/src/study/mod.rs` creates tables: collections, legacy_sources, snapshots, artifacts, sessions, reviews, review_events, attempts) + media under `<vault>/.prism/study/media`.
> - One multiplexed command `study_request(vault_path, action, payload)`, plus `study_generate` and `study_chat` for the AI work.
> - AI: the app's own configured provider (`OmniRouteConfig`, `providerId`), grounding from your vault notes via the app's own `knowledge` index, Agent tools via `agentRunner` (`edit_note` etc. — hence the Agent ON/OFF in the composer).
> - Concepts: Collection (sourceIds + revision), Snapshot (frozen source text at generation time), Artifact (table/quiz/flashcards/podcast/mindmap, versioned with `parentId` lineage), flashcard `reviews` (scheduling) and quiz `attempts`.
> - UI: `NotebookLibrary` (coverflow) → `StudyPanels` (Sources / Chat / Studio). Shares the AI assistant's conversation store (`crate::db::chat`).
> 
> **Advanced (legacy) — "Notebook" (Open Notebook)**
> - Path: `src/components/notebook/*`, `src/services/notebook.ts`, `src-tauri/src/notebook.rs`
> - It's a **client for a separate Python backend**, vendored at `notebook/upstream/open_notebook/`. The Rust side spawns and supervises it (`notebook_start`, health polling, `notebook_stop`, `notebook_status`), then proxies HTTP: `notebook_request`, `notebook_add_source` (multipart upload), `notebook_media`, `notebook_download`, `notebook_export`, `notebook_read_vault_note`, `notebook_import_copilot`.
> - Separate process, separate database, separate credentials/models. `/api/prism/drain` for background jobs, worker concurrency (1–8), page limits matching the FastAPI (`Query(le=100)`).
> - Sections: workspace / search / chats / transformations / podcasts / settings. First startup can take a minute (it's booting a server).
> - "Advanced" here means: the full Open Notebook feature set (sources, transformations, podcasts, job queue) — a superset/integration, not a more advanced UI.
> 
> **How they connect**
> - In the study workspace's overflow menu there's "Advanced Notebook" → `onOpenLegacy('workspace')` → App renders `<NotebookPage>` as the `legacy` prop. Same for the assistant: "Advanced assistant: agent and web tools" toggles `AISidebar`.

Two separate products living behind one name — that naming collision is part of why it's confusing.

| | **Regular Notebook** ("study workspace") | **Advanced Notebook** (legacy) |
|---|---|---|
| Code | `src/components/study/*`, `src/services/study.ts`, `src-tauri/src/study/` | `src/components/notebook/*`, `src/services/notebook.ts`, `src-tauri/src/notebook.rs` |
| Backend | Runs **inside the Tauri app** | A **separate Python server** (Open Notebook, vendored at `notebook/upstream/open_notebook/`) |
| Storage | The app's own SQLite: `collections`, `snapshots`, `artifacts`, `sessions`, `reviews`, `attempts` + media in `<vault>/.prism/study/media` | Its own database, owned by that server process |
| Transport | One multiplexed command, `study_request(vaultPath, action, payload)`, plus `study_generate` / `study_chat` | HTTP proxied over Rust: `notebook_request`, `notebook_add_source`, `notebook_media`, `notebook_export`, … |
| AI | Your configured route (`OmniRouteConfig` / `providerId`), grounded in vault notes via the app's own `knowledge` index; Agent tools via `agentRunner` | The server's own credentials/models — `notebook_import_copilot` copies Prism's provider *into* it |
| Startup | Instant | Spawns a server; "First startup may take a minute" |
| Sections | Sources / Chat / Studio | workspace / search / chats / transformations / podcasts / settings |

## "Advanced" is misleading

The legacy one isn't a more powerful UI — it's the **full Open Notebook integration**: file uploads, transformations, a background job queue with worker concurrency, its own podcasts/settings. The new one is Prism-native: collections of your *vault notes* (not uploads), frozen snapshots for grounding, and versioned artifacts with flashcard scheduling and quiz attempt history.

## How they meet

- **Entry**: the study workspace's overflow menu has **"Advanced Notebook"** → `onOpenLegacy('workspace')` → `App.tsx` renders `<NotebookPage>` as the `legacy` prop. The assistant has the mirror toggle ("Advanced assistant: agent and web tools" → `AISidebar`).
- **Data bridge**: the new workspace can pull a legacy source in as `legacy:<id>` (and `legacy:note:<id>`). `services/study.ts` fetches it through `NotebookClient` and writes a frozen copy into the `legacy_sources` table; Rust's `resolve()` reads it back. So a new-style collection can cite an Open Notebook source.
- **Podcast setup**: opening the podcast tool with no voice configured hands off to the legacy screens (`onOpenLegacy('podcasts')`).
- `PRODUCT_SCOPE.md` mandates preserving both — explicitly: "Do not merge storage systems as part of interface cleanup."

**The name collision:** the new workspace labels *itself* "NOTEBOOK" in the UI ("New notebook", "Back to notebooks"), while the legacy `NotebookPage` is the thing actually called "Notebook" in navigation. Worth knowing before you say "the notebook" to anyone.

My recent contrast/theming work touched the **regular** one (study workspace + shared chat, plus the shared tokens/widgets) — the legacy screens were deliberately left on their own palette, per that scope doc.

      function PodcastAudio({vaultPath,artifact:a,onRefresh,onSetup}:{vaultPath:string;artifact:Artifact;onRefresh:()=>Promise<void>;onSetup:()=>void}){
       const [client,setClient]=useState<NotebookClient|null>(null);const [profiles,setProfiles]=useState<any[]>([]);const [speakers,setSpeakers]=useState<any[]>([]);const [profile,setProfile]=useState('');const [speaker,setSpeaker]=useState('');const [error,setError]=useState('');const [busy,setBusy]=useState(false);const [url,setUrl]=useState('');
       useEffect(()=>{let alive=true;let object='';void study.request<number[]>(vaultPath,'audio',{id:a.id}).then(bytes=>{if(alive){object=URL.createObjectURL(new Blob([new Uint8Array(bytes)],{type:'audio/mpeg'}));setUrl(object);}}).catch(()=>{});return()=>{alive=false;if(object)URL.revokeObjectURL(object);};},[vaultPath,a.id,a.version]);

      const WorkerQueueControl: React.FC<{

        onChange: (v: number | undefined) => void;

        const override = normalizeWorkerConcurrency(value);
        const [text, setText] = useState(value === undefined ? '' : String(value));

          if (text.trim() === '') {

          if (n === null) return; // keep the invalid text visible with the hint

      #[tauri::command]
      async fn link_notebook_session(
          app_handle: tauri::AppHandle,
          notebook_session_id: String,
          title: String,
          notebook_id: Option<String>,
          source_id: Option<String>,
          model: Option<String>,
      ) -> Result<db::chat::ChatSession, String> {
          tauri::async_runtime::spawn_blocking(move || {
              let scope = knowledge::current(&app_handle)?;
              let conn = db::init_db(&app_handle)?;
              db::chat::link_notebook_session(
                  &conn,
                  &scope.vault_id,
                  &notebook_session_id,
                  &title,
                  notebook_id.as_deref(),
                  source_id.as_deref(),
                  model.as_deref(),
              )
          })
          .await
          .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?
      }
      
      #[tauri::command]
      async fn unlink_notebook_session(
          app_handle: tauri::AppHandle,
          notebook_session_id: String,
      ) -> Result<bool, String> {
          tauri::async_runtime::spawn_blocking(move || {
              let scope = knowledge::current(&app_handle)?;
              let conn = db::init_db(&app_handle)?;
              db::chat::unlink_notebook_session(&conn, &scope.vault_id, &notebook_session_id)
          })
          .await
          .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?
      }

  content: |
      /// Fully closes Prism and starts a fresh instance of the current executable.
      /// Unlike a webview reload, this tears down and restarts the whole Tauri
      /// process so anything initialized at startup (watcher, DB caches, etc.) is
      /// rebuilt. The new process is detached so it survives the exit of this one.
      #[tauri::command]
      async fn relaunch_app(
          app: tauri::AppHandle,
          notebook_state: tauri::State<'_, notebook::NotebookState>,
      ) -> Result<(), String> {
          notebook::shutdown(&notebook_state).await;
          let exe = std::env::current_exe().map_err(|e| format!("Failed to resolve executable: {e}"))?;
          std::process::Command::new(exe)
              .stdin(Stdio::null())
              .stdout(Stdio::null())
              .stderr(Stdio::null())
              .spawn()
              .map_err(|e| format!("Failed to relaunch: {e}"))?;
          app.exit(0);
          Ok(())
      }
      
      /// Searches the web via DuckDuckGo's HTML-lite endpoint (no API key needed)
      /// and returns the top results. The response body is parsed with the scraper
      /// crate — the HTML structure is simple enough for CSS selectors.
      #[tauri::command]
      async fn web_search(app: tauri::AppHandle, query: String) -> Result<Vec<WebSearchResult>, String> {
          let consent_query = query.clone();
          tauri::async_runtime::spawn_blocking(move || {
              knowledge::models::authorize(
                  &app,
                  "https://html.duckduckgo.com",
                  "WEB_SEARCH",
                  &consent_query,
                  false,
                  false,
              )
          })
          .await
          .map_err(|e| e.to_string())??;
          let url = format!(
              "https://html.duckduckgo.com/html/?q={}",
              urlencoding::encode(&query)
          );
      
          let body = reqwest::get(&url)
              .await
              .map_err(|e| format!("Network error: {e}"))?
              .text()
              .await
              .map_err(|e| format!("Failed to read response: {e}"))?;
      
          let document = Html::parse_document(&body);
          let link_sel = Selector::parse(".result__a").map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
          let snippet_sel = Selector::parse(".result__snippet").map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
          let container_sel = Selector::parse(".result.results_links").map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;

      pub async fn study_export(app:tauri::AppHandle,vault_path:String,id:String,format:String)->Result<bool,String>{

          let script=temp.path().join("export.py");std::fs::write(&script,include_str!("../../../notebook/study_export.py")).map_err(error)?;

          let log=std::fs::File::create(temp.path().join("error.log")).map_err(error)?;
          let mut process=Command::new(python).arg("-B").arg(script).arg(&input).arg(&output).env("PYTHONPATH",root.join("lib")).env("PYTHONNOUSERSITE","1").stdout(Stdio::null()).stderr(log).spawn().map_err(error)?;
          let start=std::time::Instant::now();loop{if let Some(status)=process.try_wait().map_err(error)?{if !status.success(){let detail=std::fs::read_to_string(temp.path().join("error.log")).unwrap_or_default();return Err(format!("Export failed. Ensure the bundled study export dependencies are installed. {}",detail.chars().take(1000).collect::<String>()));}break;}if check(&app,&s).is_err()||start.elapsed().as_secs()>60{let _=process.kill();let _=process.wait();return Err("Export cancelled or timed out; the saved material is unchanged".into());}std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(100));}

/// Create or refresh the linked entry for a Notebook backend session so it
/// shows up in the shared library. Never touches copilot-owned rows.
pub fn link_notebook_session(
    conn: &Connection,
    vault_id: &str,
    notebook_session_id: &str,
    title: &str,
    notebook_id: Option<&str>,
    source_id: Option<&str>,
    model: Option<&str>,
) -> Result<ChatSession, String> {
    let title = title.trim();
    let title: String = if title.is_empty() {
        "Conversation".into()
    } else {
        title.chars().take(120).collect()
    };
    conn.execute(
        "INSERT INTO chat_sessions(id, vault_id, title, origin, notebook_session_id, notebook_id, source_id, model)
         VALUES (?1, ?2, ?3, 'notebook', ?4, ?5, ?6, ?7)
         ON CONFLICT(vault_id, notebook_session_id) DO UPDATE SET
           title=excluded.title, notebook_id=excluded.notebook_id,
           source_id=excluded.source_id, model=excluded.model, updated_at=unixepoch()",
        params![
            uuid::Uuid::new_v4().to_string(),
            vault_id,
            title,
            notebook_session_id,
            notebook_id,
            source_id,

      /// Clamp a stored override into range; returns None when unset so callers
      /// fall back to the default instead of breaking queue behavior.
      pub fn effective_worker_concurrency(override_value: Option<u32>) -> u32 {
          match override_value {
              Some(n) if n >= MIN_WORKER_CONCURRENCY && n <= MAX_WORKER_CONCURRENCY => n,
              _ => DEFAULT_WORKER_CONCURRENCY,
          }
      }

              let mut json = serde_json::to_value(RuntimeConfig::default()).unwrap();
              json.as_object_mut().unwrap().remove("notebook");
              let restored: RuntimeConfig = serde_json::from_value(json).unwrap();
              assert!(!restored.notebook.embed_by_default);
              assert_eq!(restored.notebook.source_panel_width, 260);

              assert_eq!(

                  DEFAULT_WORKER_CONCURRENCY
              );
              assert_eq!(restored.appearance.startup_view, "editor");
          }
      
          #[test]
          fn focused_defaults_preserve_existing_appearance_choices() {

                  let config: AppearanceConfig = serde_json::from_value(appearance).unwrap();
                  assert_eq!(config.startup_view, "editor");

              for view in ["editor", "graph", "split", "topics", "notebook"] {

                  let reopened: AppearanceConfig = serde_json::from_str(&serde_json::to_string(&config).unwrap()).unwrap();
                  assert_eq!(reopened.startup_view, view);
                  assert_eq!(reopened.default_graph_mode, "3d");
              }
          }
      
          #[test]
          fn worker_concurrency_override_clamps_to_safe_range() {
              // No override (incl. old settings files without the key) → default.
              assert_eq!(
                  effective_worker_concurrency(None),
                  DEFAULT_WORKER_CONCURRENCY
              );
              assert_eq!(effective_worker_concurrency(Some(4)), 4);
              // Out-of-range / zero values never break queue behavior.
              assert_eq!(
                  effective_worker_concurrency(Some(0)),
                  DEFAULT_WORKER_CONCURRENCY
              );
              assert_eq!(
                  effective_worker_concurrency(Some(99)),
                  DEFAULT_WORKER_CONCURRENCY
              );
              // Serde round-trip: missing key and explicit null both mean "no override".

              let nulled: NotebookConfig =

              assert_eq!(nulled.worker_concurrency, None);

      use super::*;
      use std::process::{Command,Stdio};
      #[tauri::command]
      pub async fn study_export(app:tauri::AppHandle,vault_path:String,id:String,format:String)->Result<bool,String>{
       let s=scope(&app,&vault_path)?;
       tauri::async_runtime::spawn_blocking(move||{
        let c=db(&s)?;let a=artifacts::get(&c,&id)?;
        let allowed=match a.kind.as_str(){"table"=>vec!["csv","pdf"],"quiz"=>vec!["md","pdf"],"flashcards"=>vec!["csv","apkg","pdf"],"podcast"=>vec!["mp3","md","pdf"],"slides"=>vec!["pptx","pdf"],"mindmap"=>vec!["svg","md","pdf"],_=>vec![]};
        if !allowed.contains(&format.as_str()){return Err("Unsupported export format".into());}
        let snapshot=load_snapshot(&c,&a.snapshot_id)?;    let temp=tempfile::tempdir().map_err(error)?;let output=temp.path().join(format!("export.{format}"));
        if format=="mp3" {
          let audio=s.root.join(".prism/study/media").join(format!("{}.mp3",a.id));operations::validate(&s.root,&audio)?;
          if !audio.is_file(){return Err("Generate and save the podcast audio first".into());}std::fs::copy(audio,&output).map_err(error)?;
        }else{
          return Err("Export for this format needs the Notebook runtime that shipped with the retired Advanced Notebook. It is no longer bundled, so the saved material is unchanged. Podcast audio (mp3) still exports.".into());
        }
        check(&app,&s)?;let name:String=a.title.chars().filter(|ch|!['/','\\',':','\0'].contains(ch)).take(100).collect();
        let Some(destination)=rfd::FileDialog::new().set_file_name(format!("{name}.{format}")).add_filter("Study export",&[format.as_str()]).save_file()else{return Ok(false)};
        check(&app,&s)?;let bytes=std::fs::read(output).map_err(error)?;let parent=destination.parent().ok_or("Invalid export destination")?;let mut staged=tempfile::NamedTempFile::new_in(parent).map_err(error)?;use std::io::Write;staged.write_all(&bytes).map_err(error)?;staged.as_file().sync_all().map_err(error)?;staged.persist(&destination).map_err(error)?;Ok(true)
       }).await.map_err(error)?
      }

      # Product focus and compatibility
      
      Prism helps people turn their own notes and sources into connected, searchable knowledge they control. Its core workflow is capture → find → connect → ask → save, supporting knowledge work, research, and study.
      
      ## Simplification without removal
      
      Keep core actions easy to reach and group secondary tools behind clearly labeled navigation. Grouping a feature does not disable it or reduce its support. Preserve existing features, user data, saved preferences, shortcuts, and access to Notebook, graph views, podcasts, transformations, and advanced AI configuration. Do not merge storage systems or change AI permissions as part of interface cleanup.
      
      ## Planned work remains in scope
      
      Open Notebook integration, OpenClaw, the V2 architecture, and study tools remain eligible to continue under their established specifications. This document neither implements nor redefines those projects, and does not claim that planned capabilities have shipped. There is no blanket feature freeze.
      
      ## Evaluating additions
      
      For each future addition, document:
      
      - The knowledge, research, or study workflow it improves and evidence of the user need.
      - Why existing functionality cannot adequately address that need.
      - Its navigation and onboarding impact, plus ongoing maintenance cost.
      - How it preserves existing data, privacy choices, and compatibility.
      
      Prefer improving or connecting existing workflows before adding a separate destination. Broad integrations or new product categories need the same justification; their availability alone is not a reason to add them.
      
  referencedBy: {}

Do not merge storage systems or change AI permissions as part of interface cleanup.\n\n\"Notebook\" means the Prism-native notebook: the notebook library, its Sources / Chat / Studio workspace, and the study materials generated from selected vault notes. There is one notebook.\n\n## Removed: the Open Notebook integration\n\nThe Advanced Notebook — the vendored Open Notebook server (Python runtime, `notebook_*` commands, its own database, upload pipeline, transformations and podcast screens) — has been removed deliberately. It is no longer \"planned work\", no longer bundled, and is not a candidate for reinstatement under this document.\n\nWhat this cost, recorded so the trade-off stays visible:\n\n- Open Notebook **sources** (file uploads), **transformations**, and its **podcast/job screens** are gone. Notebook podcast audio generation went with them; podcast artifacts keep their transcript and any audio already saved.\n- Study-material **export** was implemented by running the bundled Python, so only podcast audio (`.mp3`, plain Rust copy) still exports. Other formats report the missing runtime instead of failing silently.\n- Existing Open Notebook data is **not deleted** — it stays on disk — but Prism no longer reaches it. Conversations previously linked into the chat library keep their rows and remain visible; they adopt Prism's own stored messages and can no longer be refreshed from the server.\n\n## Planned work remains in scope\n\nOpenClaw, the V2 architecture, and study tools remain eligible to continue under their established specifications. This document neither implements nor redefines those projects, and does not claim that planned capabilities have shipped. There is no blanket feature freeze.",
